comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: 2026-10-21: fixed on main in 371ce7d0, the narrow option: unread_after no longer counts a message from @muster addressed to other members; everything else still counts. Test in muster-msg's telling.rs fails without it. MIP-4 section 4 and docs/cli/msg.md say so. Full gate pending (disk).

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From tooling feedback, 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-18, 0.16.1-dev on the Mac, four sightings. @muster's notices to a maker about its helper ("went idle without posting to you", "is blocked at a dialog") are posted in the group the two share. The helper's next `muster msg post` to its maker is then refused with `2 unread messages in <group>; read them ... then post again`, because the guard in `Service::post` (`crates/muster-msg/src/service.rs`, `unread_after`) counts every message after the author's cursor, whoever it was addressed to.

Costs seen: a time-critical post took an extra round trip. A Codex helper whose brief said "post, then stop" printed "Muster rejected it ... I stopped as requested" and ended its turn, so its report never arrived, and its maker learned of it only from the next idle notice. A peer pane, not a helper, hit the same with a "blocked at a dialog" notice about its own plan dialog.

The guard exists so a model does not post on stale context (MIP-4, section 4). A notice about you addressed to somebody else is not context you need before posting. Options: leave @muster's messages addressed to other members out of the count; or leave out every message not addressed to the author, which changes the guard for agents' posts too and wants a look at MIP-4 first.
title: A notice @muster addresses to one member refuses the other members' posts
